messages:
alex: Quick Q about embeddings API contract as we stabilize SDKs — trying to finalize behavior for weird inputs so it's non-breaking. Specifically: empty string vs null, empty items in a batch (e.g. [] or ""), and items that exceed model context (token truncation). Also need to agree on output shape per item (vector vs null vs error payload). Example request below — what's our intended response shape?

sam_k: Short version: preserve input order, return one entry per input. But we need to decide if empty string -> vector or null. Historically there was some variance.

maria_g: Ops note: for Dedicated/Private customers we promised backwards compat. Proposal: (1) always preserve order and include per-item metadata, (2) empty string -> deterministic embedding (so clients that cosim/compare still get something), (3) null (explicit JSON null) -> treated as an error for that item -> return null vector + error code, (4) if we truncate input -> return vector for truncated text and set "truncated":true + include "original_length" or tokens if available.

alex: Would deterministic vector-for-"" break anyone relying on null-as-absent? I recall one internal consumer used null to mean skip. @taylor any product constraints?

taylor: PM view: prefer non-breaking for public API. Deterministic vector for empty string is fine. For explicit null, prefer an explicit per-item error object so SDKs can surface it without changing HTTP status. Also prefer we keep HTTP 200 and per-item error fields. Top-level response should include model id + batch id so clients can log reproducibility.

ops-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-api/pull/512 — implements per-item metadata and flags. CI: tests passing. :white_check_mark:

sam_k: Example of proposed request/response (short):

```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "embed-1",
  "input": ["hello", "", null, "<very long text that might exceed tokens>"]
}

200 OK
{
  "model": "embed-1",
  "batch_id": "b-123",
  "data": [
    {"index": 0, "vector": [0.01, -0.23, ...], "truncated": false},
    {"index": 1, "vector": [0.00, 0.02, ...], "truncated": false, "note": "empty-string"},
    {"index": 2, "vector": null, "error": "null_item"},
    {"index": 3, "vector": [0.12, -0.05, ...], "truncated": true, "original_tokens": 1200}
  ]
}
```

maria_g: Implementation detail: runtime currently sometimes returns a zero vector for empty string due to an early-exit fastpath. We need to ensure the vector is deterministic across backends (e.g. quantized vs fp16) — caching the empty-string embedding at model onboarding time would help. Also we should avoid generating an error for empty string unless it's explicitly null.

alex: Decision for this thread: 1) keep order, 2) empty string -> deterministic vector (document as "empty-string" note), 3) explicit null -> per-item error + null vector, 4) truncation -> vector + "truncated": true + token/char metadata where available, 5) HTTP 200 always, with top-level model and batch_id. @sam_k handle SDK stubs, @maria_g add runtime compatibility tests, I'll draft changelog entry.

sam_k: I'll update SDK stubs + add integration tests for mixed input types and truncation flags. Filed issue #789 and added a unit test in PR.

taylor: Agree. Also please add a quick section in the changelog clarifying migration notes for clients that previously treated empty strings as missing.

alex: Awesome, thanks all :thumbsup:
